newsitem.title: FRANCE: Quarter of Eurotunnel debt traded - Ponsolle.
newsitem.headline: Quarter of Eurotunnel debt traded - Ponsolle.

text.p: Between 20-25 percent of the 70 billion francs of junior bank loans owed by Eurotunnel Plc/SA has been sold by lenders on the secondary market, French executive chairman Patrick Ponsolle told Reuters.

Eurotunnel wanted to clarify the composition of its loan syndicate and opened a window for the month of April for banks to formalise their sales, he said after a news conference on Thursday on 1996 results.
The amount of debt traded should not change significantly by the end of the month, he said. The information came from lending banks.

One of the advantages of allowing the official debt sales was to allow banks opposed to the debt restructuring deal to leave the syndicate, Ponsolle said, adding that this was not the aim of the move.

Under the standstill agreement, invoked when Eurotunnel froze interest payments in September 1995, banks were prevented from formally selling their debt through assigning the loans. But that did not stop banks selling loans through cumbersome sub-participations, which kept their names on as the lender on record.
Eurotunnel must get approval from all its lenders for the restructuring, which it says may be agreed in the autumn.

One debt specialist said the U.S. funds which bought the loans would likely go along with the restructuring deal and take a capital gain when a deal is agreed among the syndicate, rather than take an active role in negotiating better terms.
Eurotunnel debt was priced around 40-45 percent of nominal value in the secondary market, but that was probably inflated as there was more money chasing the debt on offer, the debt trader said.

Eurotunnel said on Thursday a steering group of six leading banks had agreed the detailed restructuring terms. The company presented the package to the second tier of 21 instructing banks in a meeting which went to midnight on Wednesday, a source close to the company said.
